Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines stable domain identity and continuity for a Financial Entity; it does not define a database key or storage record.

Requirements

  • ENTITY-IDENTITY-001 — A Financial Entity MUST have an identifier unique within its declared identity scope.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Provides context

    Balanced totals do not establish the validity of an economic event ↗

    Mikhaylov Bogdan; Omorov Akzholbek; Izripov Iusup

    Stable financial-subject identity is useful context when discussing duplicated economic events. These clauses do not define balanced postings or accounting recognition; the ledger claim remains deferred.

    Scope and limitations

    The paper explicitly notes balanced errors but cites Ellerman; the original cited account has not been checked. A reviewer-created duplicate posting can preserve totals, but is not a Core operation or a financial test executed here.

  • ENTITY-IDENTITY-002 — The identifier MUST remain stable for the Financial Entity's entire lifecycle.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Provides context

    Balanced totals do not establish the validity of an economic event ↗

    Mikhaylov Bogdan; Omorov Akzholbek; Izripov Iusup

    Stable financial-subject identity is useful context when discussing duplicated economic events. These clauses do not define balanced postings or accounting recognition; the ledger claim remains deferred.

    Scope and limitations

    The paper explicitly notes balanced errors but cites Ellerman; the original cited account has not been checked. A reviewer-created duplicate posting can preserve totals, but is not a Core operation or a financial test executed here.

  • ENTITY-IDENTITY-003 — Identifiers MUST be opaque; consumers MUST NOT infer mutable domain facts from their format.
  • ENTITY-IDENTITY-004 — Revisions, versions, and display numbers MUST NOT replace stable identity unless a composing specification explicitly makes them identical and immutable.
  • ENTITY-IDENTITY-005 — Two distinct entities MUST NOT share the same identifier within the same scope.
  • ENTITY-IDENTITY-006 — Import or migration MUST preserve identity or record an explicit identity mapping.
  • ENTITY-IDENTITY-007 — The bounded Entity definition MUST explicitly supply a nonempty string identity scope. Omission, null, or a malformed scope MUST use FINKORE_ENTITY_INVALID_IDENTITY. This fixture requirement MUST NOT be interpreted as a global identity registry or a production serialization format.

Core 2.0 refines import mapping in Entity Import. That refinement does not create a global registry or permit Source Identity to replace stable FinKore Entity identity.

Invariants

A Mutation, Transition, or other domain operation must not silently create a new identity for the same continuing Financial Entity.

Example

The following JSON is illustrative and non-normative. It does not prescribe common serialized member names or an identifier format.

{
  "entityType": "expense",
  "entityId": "exp-52"
}

Invalid Examples

  • Changing a Financial Entity identifier when its State changes.
  • Using a mutable title as the sole identity.

Open Questions

  • Should the specification define a common identity scope model across entity types and tenants?
